svg.title: Kickl encryption map: where plaintext exists
svg.desc: Three lanes showing at-rest, in-memory and on-the-wire data, the key hierarchy, and an inventory of where plaintext exists.
svg.text: Where plaintext exists, and where it does not. Slice build · 2026-10-27 · AES-256-GCM everywhere symmetric; hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 for the CA.

g.text: publicKey wrapped under a name-derived key
opens for any Kickl reader by design
the phonebook is public by design
no page content is stored here
PFS query on wire is ciphertext
byte[] wiped; UI string dropped on Lock
does NOT see: name, tag, or status
RSA-3072 signs; peer id pinned; P-256 only
one-time keys die with the link
system browser + TLS only (BTC shop + CA too)
no registry, no seals, no Kickl keys
TLS 1.3 to a key pinned in the signed endpoint
sees: that a mail device is at that address
no plain http · no downgrade · 16 connections
server still decides who is in the room ← limit

svg.text: Claiming a name is paid at the BTC shop; the CA watches and seals; a game is a sandbox with nothing to reach.

g.text: shop signs site · order · claim no. · dates · token
RSA-3072; the shop key is pinned on first contact
token = 32 random bytes; the file holder owns the name
checked again every time you press edit
the receipt crosses the network over TLS only ← limit
owner binding: shop signs HMAC(passphrase) into it
bought without a passphrase: the file owns the name
claimed: publishing needs the certificate + passphrase
unclaimed names stay free; a re-claim retires the old
hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65: both halves must verify
domain-separated: issuer cert · seal · log head · revocations
RFC 6962 Merkle log; the seal carries its inclusion proof
the seal is public: it holds no token, only SHA-256(token)
published with the site; outside the integrity hash
root public key is built into the browser
the root private key is not on the CA server
root revokes issuers + claims; an issuer, claims only
the CA refuses clashing, stale or expired receipts
the issuing key is online (bounded by its 90 days) ← limit
the module is a sealed blob (public or protected)
imports nothing: no clock, network, files or host calls
fuel per frame · memory cap · a trap halts only the game
starts only when you press play; stops when you leave
game memory + its 240x160 picture: RAM only
unclaimed names: 512 KiB · 8 MiB · 10 M per frame
claimed names: 2 MiB · 32 MiB · 40 M per frame
a game can still draw anything, even misleading text
a heavy game slows the page, though it cannot freeze it

svg.text: Read this as the complete list. Anything not here is ciphertext or derived material.

g.text: master, session and doc key after unlock
page markup + the one region you revealed
blob text (byte[] wiped, decoded string is not)
ownership token while it is checked or sent to the CA
a running game: its memory and its picture
the cached shop and CA public keys
page title, blob mime and size in doc.json
registry name / status / owner / badge ids
stego seed in the PNG tEXt chunk
anything you redirect CLI output into
CA seals (public, no token) and the revocation list
pinned shop key · CA public keys · title.json (hash only)
the CA ledger: sites, claim numbers, times, log positions
master key · session key · doc key
PFS lookup traffic · mesh frames · mail on the wire
page markup · protected blobs (need the access key)
ownership certificates · saved .kcert copies · game saves · FreeChat keys
a compromised OS, firmware, or USB port
the TLS link to the BTC shop and the CA (receipt travels here)
a copied .kcert that was bought without a passphrase
Rule: if a byte is not in the green or amber lists, it is not plaintext.
Public pages are sealed at rest but open for any reader by design; only the access key protects protected blobs.
A seal proves the CA saw and logged a genuine receipt, not who the buyer is. The token reaches the CA over TLS only; the CA keeps a hash. A passphrase (owner binding) locks the file.
